knowledge_point.title: Computing a Tangent or Cotangent Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.:question/problem:
![](images/96/96b22799c75a4b19df4c6bddf8b63d11a7d0cab8a0cc481b8466a29eb1a2af15.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $tan⁡\theta .$
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/21/21170c11aa5ff0ab39b86f94588e5e8a0fa178d0c34b9aa1774ee9f07a4d0812.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=cos⁡\theta ,\,y=sin⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $y=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
sin⁡\theta =\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{45}{49}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{4}{49}} \\  & =\pm \frac{2}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =\frac{2}{7}.$

Finally, knowing that $tan⁡\theta =\frac{sin⁡\theta }{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
tan⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7})}{(\frac{2}{7})}=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}.
$$

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{8}.
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{1}{8})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{1}{64}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{63}{64}} \\  & =\pm \frac{3\sqrt{7}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{3\sqrt{7}}{8}.$

Finally, knowing that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{3\sqrt{7}}{8})}{(\frac{1}{8})}=3\sqrt{7}.

$$

$$
tan⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{9}{15})}{(\frac{12}{15})}=\frac{9}{12}.

knowledge_point.title: Computing a Tangent or Cotangent Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186110758/assets/c35c204dd375ea964fe7b9362c6fc4af4aea93cac6404a237f989e684ede59a0.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{\sqrt{26}}{6},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $tan⁡\theta .$
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186110758/assets/d1a7130b7aa69e3fac89cbfaff79c9e1d8101c025735449444a1e3bbcb269afd.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=cos⁡\theta ,\,y=sin⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $y=\frac{\sqrt{26}}{6}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
sin⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{26}}{6}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{26}}{6}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{\sqrt{26}}{6})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{26}{36}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{10}{36}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{10}}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{10}}{6}.$

Knowing that $tan⁡\theta =\frac{sin⁡\theta }{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
tan⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{26}}{6})}{(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{6})}=\frac{\sqrt{26}}{\sqrt{10}}.
$$

Finally, we rationalize the denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}tan⁡\theta  & =\frac{\sqrt{26}}{\sqrt{10}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{26}}{\sqrt{10}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{10}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{26\cdot 10}}{10} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{260}}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{\sqrt{38}}{8},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $tan⁡\theta .$
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186110758/assets/7af56feaf755787df2e115b7f001e8aa90b4a1f55bd5b563edfd2707289d5417.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=cos⁡\theta ,\,y=sin⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $y=\frac{\sqrt{38}}{8}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
sin⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{38}}{8}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{38}}{8}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{\sqrt{38}}{8})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{38}{64}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{26}{64}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{26}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{26}}{8}.$

Knowing that $tan⁡\theta =\frac{sin⁡\theta }{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
tan⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{38}}{8})}{(\frac{\sqrt{26}}{8})}=\frac{\sqrt{38}}{\sqrt{26}}.
$$

Finally, we rationalize the denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}tan⁡\theta  & =\frac{\sqrt{38}}{\sqrt{26}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{38}}{\sqrt{26}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{26}}{\sqrt{26}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{38\cdot 26}}{26} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{988}}{26}\end{aligned}
$$
